title: Weighing the hopper in one scan
statement: An S7-300 runs the Blender function block below once a scan. Its three load cells read $0$ to $27648$ for $0$ to $500$ kg, and the recipe wants $120$, $80$ and $120$ kg. For each set of raw values, fill in the weight in the hopper, how full the batch is, and how many $25$ kg bags it fills, rounded to the nearest bag.
given: load cells: raw $0$ to $27648$ is $0$ to $500$ kg

artefact.caption: One scan, three sets of raw values

steps.title: Weigh the silos
steps.note: The FOR loop scales each load cell with ToKg, $\text{kg} = \frac{\text{raw}}{27648} \cdot 500$, and adds it up: $117.1875 + 78.125 + 117.1875 = 312.5$ kg.

steps.title: How full the batch is
steps.note: The recipe adds up to $120 + 80 + 120 = 320$ kg, so the hopper holds $\frac{312.5}{320} \cdot 100 = 97.66$ % of it.

steps.title: Bags to fill
steps.note: $\frac{312.5}{25} = 12.5$ bags, which the Professor rounds up to $13$. REAL_TO_INT on a real S7 rounds a tie to the even number, $12$: the exam wants $13$.

answer: At raw values $6480$, $4320$ and $6480$ the hopper holds $312.5$ kg, $97.66$ % of the batch, which the exam counts as $13$ bags.

stated: an S7-300 with three load cells, $1$, $2$ and $3$

divergences.note: REAL_TO_INT rounds $12.5$ to the even number on a real S7, so the CPU holds $12$; the Professor's answer, $13$, is the exam's.
